solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Man at wicket, ignorant, old, causing big beam for attackers

parts.note: the player at the wicket in cricket is the batter
an obsolete word for ignorant, as listed in Chambers

explanation.surface: A cricketer at the crease, dim and ageing, somehow provokes a fearsome weapon for an assault.
explanation.walkthrough: INGRAM is an archaic adjective meaning ignorant; Azed relies on Chambers for such words.
explanation.definitionFit: A battering ram is a heavy log swung by besiegers to break down gates or walls.

clue.text: Bout ref's disrupted includes part of speech discouraging extremism

definitions.note: describes the ban rather than naming it; the answer is a noun

indicators.note: the jumbled letters hold another piece inside them
something disrupted is thrown out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters taken as written, apostrophe dropped
a verb is one of the parts of speech

explanation.surface: A boxing referee's speech is interrupted by something meant to calm fanatics.
explanation.walkthrough: VERB sits inside the jumble after its sixth letter. The answer is German, literally a professional ban.
explanation.definitionFit: A Berufsverbot was a West German ban on employing political radicals in public service, meant to deter extremism.

clue.text: Bearer's chest strap, point being to limit lump shifting

indicators.note: to limit something is to hem it in, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: a tine is a prong or point, as on a fork

indicators.note: letters that are shifting move about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written before rearranging

explanation.surface: A porter's harness exists so that a heavy load does not slide about.
explanation.definitionFit: A tumpline is a strap passing over the forehead or chest of a porter to support a load on the back.

clue.text: Tissue left among contents of bag?

indicators.note: a thing placed among others sits inside them

parts.note: a teabag holds tea; the question mark flags the indirect hint
L is the standard abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Someone checks what remains of the tissues stuffed in a handbag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tissue' and 'bag' suggest handkerchiefs in a handbag, but the bag is a teabag.
explanation.definitionFit: Tela is an anatomical term for a web-like layer of tissue in the body.

clue.text: Moderation in dealing with a child

parts.note: re means concerning or with regard to
taken as written
a son is a male child

explanation.surface: Parenting advice: be temperate when handling your offspring.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests reasoning with a child, but the word is split into three short pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Reason means sensible limits or moderation, as in the phrase 'within reason'.

clue.text: Since at odds about marriage, refinements will be needed

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go around another piece
letters at odds are in disagreement and out of their usual order

parts.note: taken as written before rearranging
marriage is a tie, the knot that binds a couple

explanation.surface: A quarrelling couple will need to observe some polite formalities to keep their marriage going.
explanation.definitionFit: Niceties are fine points or subtle refinements of manners or detail.

clue.text: Bird of prey, catch about dead

indicators.note: one word is wrapped around the other, standing about it

parts.note: a catch is a round sung in parts, much like a glee
D is the standard abbreviation for dead

explanation.surface: A hawk seizes a carcass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Catch' suggests seizing prey, but it is the musical sense: a catch and a glee are both part-songs.
explanation.definitionFit: Glede is an old and dialect name for the kite, a bird of prey.

clue.text: Branch of the forces, mostly excellent in purpose

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: your aim is your purpose

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: rare can mean excellent, as in a rare old time

explanation.surface: A division of the military is described as largely superb in its sense of purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: The air arm is the part of a country's armed forces that operates aircraft.

clue.text: A limp's aggravated, bond showing wrong setting

indicators.note: something aggravated is worsened and stirred up, so these letters are thrown about

parts.note: the letters taken as written, apostrophe dropped
cement is a bonding agent; to bond is to cement

explanation.surface: An injured leg has been made worse by a cast that was badly set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setting' looks medical, a bone being set, but here it means placement.
explanation.definitionFit: Misplacement is putting something in the wrong place, a wrong setting or position.

clue.text: Some former African money, likewise of old including returned Romanian ditto

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the word is read from right to left
the outer word takes another piece inside it

parts.note: eke is an archaic word for also or likewise
the leu is the Romanian currency unit, hence 'ditto' for money

explanation.surface: A collector's list of obsolete currencies: an African coin, then a Romanian one, likewise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ditto' repeats 'money', telling you to think of a Romanian currency rather than a Romanian person.
explanation.definitionFit: The ekuele was the currency of Equatorial Guinea before it adopted the CFA franc.

clue.text: Melanesian king over area more than half stripped

indicators.note: keeping more than half of a word means cutting off its tail
in a down entry, over means placed above the following pieces

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
A is the abbreviation for area
stripped means unclothed

explanation.surface: A Pacific islander's ruler presides over a region largely laid bare.
explanation.walkthrough: Three of the five letters of the word for stripped are kept, which is more than half.
explanation.definitionFit: Kanak is the name for an indigenous Melanesian of New Caledonia.

clue.text: International c-cap recalled? It's baggy for Australian

definitions.note: a playful cryptic definition of a bag

indicators.note: something recalled is called back, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: I is the abbreviation for international
the stutter on cap is copied onto its synonym lid, doubling the first letter

explanation.surface: A stammered mention of an international cap sounds like a sportsman being remembered for his loose kit.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphenated stutter in c-cap tells you to stutter the synonym too.
explanation.definitionFit: A dilli or dilly bag is an Australian Aboriginal bag woven from grass or fibre.

clue.text: Early minstrelsy, a very pleasant thing

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an obsolete sense of music or minstrelsy
second meaning: something delightful, as in 'it went like a ...'

explanation.surface: Old-time songs by wandering musicians were a real delight.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is obsolete, recorded in Chambers as joy, mirth or minstrelsy.
explanation.definitionFit: The word once meant music and mirth, and today names anything wonderful, like a holiday that was perfect.

clue.text: Buffoons race crazily in warm clothing

indicators.note: the jumble is placed inside the clothing

parts.note: furs are warm garments

indicators.note: acting crazily means behaving wildly, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written before rearranging

explanation.surface: Clowns in fur coats run about madly.
explanation.definitionFit: A farceur is a joker or performer of farce, so the plural means comic clowns.

clue.text: Classy notary always gets to make good by recompense

parts.note: U means upper-class, as in U and non-U
NP stands for notary public
ay or aye is an old word for always

explanation.surface: An upmarket lawyer is always expected to pay compensation.
explanation.walkthrough: U and non-U were labels for upper-class and other usage in British English.
explanation.definitionFit: Unpay is a Shakespearean verb meaning to undo or make amends for something by paying it back.

clue.text: The Scots abandon pump, hoarding last of water

indicators.note: to hoard is to keep stored up within, so one piece is held inside another
last of picks out the final letter of the next word to be held inside

parts.note: a pump is a plimsoll, which in the west of Britain is called a dap
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Scotsmen give up on a pump that has trapped the remaining water.
explanation.walkthrough: A pump and a dap are both names for a light canvas gym shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: Drap is the Scots form of drop, and to drop a plan is to abandon it.

clue.text: Sort of dinghy afloat at sea, circling small warship

indicators.note: circling means going all the way around another piece
at sea means confused and adrift, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written before rearranging
TB is short for torpedo boat

explanation.surface: A little boat bobbing on the ocean sails around a tiny naval vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A faltboat is a collapsible canoe or folding boat, from German Faltboot.

clue.text: Explode with rage, as Mary, the Queen, about mixed dish served up (8, two words)

indicators.note: the letters for Mary go about the dish

parts.note: BV stands for Blessed Virgin, a title of Mary

indicators.note: in a down entry, served up means brought upwards, so read from the bottom

parts.note: an olio is a stew of mixed ingredients
ER is the royal cipher, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: Like the Queen of Scots, a monarch rages at a muddled meal brought to table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mary, the Queen' reads as Mary Queen of Scots, but it is two pieces: the Blessed Virgin and the royal cipher.
explanation.definitionFit: To boil over is to lose one's temper, as a pot spills when heated too much.

clue.text: Savoury pastries made from irish pork (recipe not included)

indicators.note: something made from ingredients reworks them, so these letters are rearranged
a letter not included is left out of the mix

parts.note: the letters taken as written
R is the abbreviation for recipe, as on prescriptions

explanation.surface: Pastries are cooked from Irish pork, though the method is not written down.
explanation.walkthrough: One of the two Rs goes before the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Piroshki are small Russian pastries or turnovers with a savoury filling.

clue.text: Family holding party as a hoax?

indicators.note: to hold something is to have it within, so one piece sits inside

parts.note: your kin are your family
a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: Relatives throw a party just to play a trick on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To kid someone on is to tease or deceive them, playing a hoax as a joke.

clue.text: I pilfer old mum's clothing, than which you can't get lower

definitions.text: than which you can't get lower
definitions.note: describes the lowest values; the answer is a plural noun

indicators.note: clothing wraps around a body, so the outer word wraps the others

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
taken as written
nim is an archaic verb meaning to steal

explanation.surface: A confession: stealing from your old mother's wardrobe is as low as anyone can sink.
explanation.definitionFit: Minima are the lowest points or least possible values, the plural of minimum.

clue.text: Curtain secreting holy books and organ valve

indicators.note: to secrete is to hide away, so one piece is concealed inside another

parts.note: a veil is a curtain or screen
NT is the New Testament

explanation.surface: A church inventory lists a curtain hiding scripture alongside a part of the organ.
explanation.definitionFit: A ventil is a valve in a wind instrument or organ that controls the air supply.

clue.text: Rising anger, endless pain — this killer had to pay

definitions.note: describes what was paid by a killer; the answer is the payment itself

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means read from the bottom up

parts.note: ire is anger

indicators.note: endless means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: an ache is a pain

explanation.surface: Mounting fury and unending suffering are the price a murderer must pay.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a sentence on a murderer, which is just what the answer was.
explanation.definitionFit: An eriach was the fine paid by a murderer to the victim's kin under old Irish law.

clue.text: Scribbled lines — such a letter requires little effort

definitions.text: such a letter requires little effort

indicators.note: scribbled writing is messy and disordered, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written before rearranging

explanation.surface: A few lines dashed off quickly hardly take any work to write.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter' suggests correspondence, but it is a letter of the alphabet as a speech sound.
explanation.definitionFit: In phonetics a lenis consonant, such as b or d, is pronounced with weak articulation.

clue.text: In matrimonial rights and duties, a right Charlie maybe

indicators.note: pieces placed in something sit inside it

parts.note: bed in Chambers can mean marriage and its rights
taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Within marriage, the husband may turn out to be a complete fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A right Charlie' is British slang for a fool, but Charlie here is a small pointed beard named after Charles I.
explanation.definitionFit: A charley or charlie is a small pointed beard, so it is one example of facial hair.

clue.text: What's soothing about the City — still?

indicators.note: one word goes about the other, enclosing it

parts.note: a balm is a soothing ointment
EC is the postcode for the City of London

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether the financial district has quietened down.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is London's financial district, whose postcodes begin EC.
explanation.definitionFit: To becalm is to make still or quiet, as wind dropping leaves a ship motionless.

clue.text: Rock cavity to treat? Drive over it

indicators.note: in a down entry, a piece placed over another sits above it

parts.note: Dr is the street-name abbreviation for Drive
to use someone well is to treat them well

explanation.surface: A cave in the rock is to be repaired, so a road is built over it.
explanation.definitionFit: A druse is a cavity in rock lined with crystals, a geode-like hollow.

clue.text: Topping part of soldier's uniform has buckled before end of fight?

indicators.note: before places the first piece ahead of the next
something buckled is bent out of shape, so the letters are twisted

parts.note: taken as written before rearranging
a KO, knockout, ends a boxing fight

explanation.surface: A soldier's headgear got crushed before the fighting finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buckled' suggests a fastened belt or strap on the uniform, but it signals a rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A shako is a tall stiff military cap with a peak and plume, worn on top of the head.

clue.text: Sediment on promontory pierced by river in beach on sheltered side (8, two words)

parts.note: lees are the dregs that settle in wine

indicators.note: a thing pierced by another has that other thrust inside it

parts.note: a hoe is a promontory or projecting point of land, as in Plymouth Hoe
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Silt deposited on a headland cut by a stream ends up on the beach away from the wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' here only means placed after: in an across entry the second piece follows the first.
explanation.definitionFit: A lee shore is the shore on the lee side of a ship, the side sheltered from the wind.

clue.text: Outrageous bit of satiric humour

indicators.note: a bit of the words is just a piece of them, so the letters sit inside

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A joke from a lampoon goes beyond the pale.
explanation.definitionFit: Rich is used of a remark that is preposterous or outrageous, as in 'that's a bit rich'.

clue.text: Response to roll-call? Notice total

parts.note: an ad is a notice or advertisement
a sum is a total

explanation.surface: A teacher reads the register and notes the overall count.
explanation.definitionFit: Adsum is Latin for 'I am present', the traditional answer when a name is called at roll-call.

clue.text: Pipe went under water by the sound of it

indicators.note: these words say the answer is heard rather than spelled

parts.note: to go under water is to duck

explanation.surface: A tube sank beneath the surface, judging by the noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A duct is a pipe or channel that carries fluid or air.

clue.text: Dutch registering speed of birds

parts.note: bat means speed or pace, as in 'at full bat'
avian means relating to birds

explanation.surface: Netherlanders record how fast birds fly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At full bat' is an informal British phrase for at top speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Batavian means Dutch, from the Batavi, a people who lived in the Netherlands in Roman times.

clue.text: Turning dry? Certainly pulled in for refreshing drinks

indicators.note: something pulled in is drawn inside another piece
turning round means facing the other way, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: sec is the wine term for dry
OK is a casual yes, certainly

explanation.surface: Getting thirsty? Of course a stop was made for cold drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Coke is a trade name for Coca-Cola, so cokes are glasses or cans of that fizzy drink.

clue.text: Howf's closed? Lot close sine die

definitions.note: an example of what the Scots adjective can describe

indicators.note: sine die is Latin for without a day, so the letter for day is removed

parts.note: your lot is your fortune or luck
a close is an end

explanation.surface: Is the pub shut? Yes, it has closed for good, with no date to reopen.
explanation.walkthrough: A howf is a Scots word for a haunt or tavern. 'Sine die' means adjourned indefinitely, but here it is read literally, the D for day going.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucken is a Scots adjective meaning shut or closed, as a howf might be.

clue.text: One exposing propositions i.e. hot matters to be solved

indicators.note: a puzzle to be solved must be worked out, so these letters need sorting

parts.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A lecturer lays out his arguments, namely burning issues that need settling.
explanation.definitionFit: A theorematist is someone who formulates or sets out theorems, which are propositions to be proved.
